description:
Join UmbraOnxy Team: NASA Space Apps 2026

We're building a research tool that reads NASA's microgravity combustion experiments (FLEX, SoFIE, ACME, SAFFIRE). It summarizes them, ranks them and answers questions about them, organized around the variables that control fire behavior: fuel, oxygen, pressure, flow, gravity, flame shape and extinction. The aim is to help people understand how fire behaves in space and what it means for crewed spacecraft and habitats.

What we've built so far

Document ingestion for NASA reports, theses and task books

AI extraction of structured experiment data, with an adjustable ranking system

A question box that answers from the sources, with cited passages

An animated Earth vs microgravity flame comparison

Tech stack

Backend: Python 3.12 and FastAPI

Data: Neon Postgres, with SQLite for local work

AI: Groq (gpt-oss-120b), with Ollama as an optional offline fallback

Frontend: plain JavaScript and Chart.js, with no framework

Hosting: AWS Lambda (SAM) and Cloudflare Pages

CI/CD: GitHub Actions

Who we're looking for

Backend and API developers

People who like working with data, retrieval and LLMs

Frontend and visualization builders

Anyone with an interest in physics, combustion or space science, even if you can't code

You don't need to be an expert in any of these. If you think you have it in you, join us.

To join: message [your name / contact link].
